It doesn't really. If you look at the current hypotheses for the formation of the first life, it's really very blurry.

An example of this is phospholipid bilayers. These very likely predated life, and are the reason that cells are cellular.

Basically you have a bunch of proteins floating around in saline solution (early oceans). These bilayer membranes form, and one side is hydrophobic, while another is hydrophilic. The hydrophobic side of the sheet pushes away from the water, and the hydrophilic pulls in. This means that the sheet rolls up into a sphere trapping saline solution inside. This creates a protected environment for any proteins (including self replicating ones) trapped in the bilayer sphere. We're getting to the point now where we realize that life is just chemistry in an environment like this. The same chemical reaction that causes rust or fire bonds oxygen to our blood cells.
